title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
description: Given a binary search tree with **unique** values and two values `p` and `q` that both exist in the tree, return the value of their **lowest common ancestor** (LCA): the deepest node that has both `p` and `q` as descendants. A node counts as a descendant of itself.

examples.explanation: A node can be an ancestor of another node.

constraints: All values are unique and p != q.
hints: Use the BST ordering: if both p and q are smaller than the current node, go left; if both are larger, go right.
The first node where they split (or equal one of them) is the answer.
